alternate_names: Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
deities: Sri Rama, Sita and Lakshmana (Ram Parivar)
festivals: Chandanotsavam (Akshaya Tritiya, April-May; the sandalwood covering is removed for one day to reveal the deity's true form)
Giri Pradakshina (Ashadha Pournami; a 32-km barefoot circumambulation of the hill by hundreds of thousands of devotees)

history.dynasty: Eastern Ganga (13th century present structure); patronage from Cholas, Vengi Chalukyas, Gajapatis and Vijayanagara (Tuluva)
history.period: Earliest inscription 1098 CE (Kulottunga Chola I); present temple consecrated 1268 CE
history.summary: Simhachalam, the Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, stands on the Simhachalam Hill Range about 300 metres above sea level near Visakhapatnam. It is one of the ashta mahakshetras of Narasimha and a rare shrine where Vishnu is worshipped in the combined form of Varaha (boar) and Narasimha (lion-man). Legend says Vishnu manifested in this form after saving his devotee Prahlada from his father Hiranyakashipu; the deity's fierce (ugra) aspect is soothed by being covered in sandalwood paste all year, with the true stone form revealed only on Akshaya Tritiya during Chandanotsavam. The earliest inscription dates to 1098 CE recording a gift under Chola king Kulottunga I, the Vengi Chalukyas renovated it in the 11th century, and the present Kalinga-style structure was built by Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I in the 13th century and consecrated by his son Bhanudeva I in 1268 CE. The temple received later patronage from the Gajapatis and the Vijayanagara kings (Krishnadevaraya visited in 1516), went through 40 years of inactivity between 1564 and 1604, and was taken over by the state government in 1949; it is administered today by the Simhachalam Devasthanam and is the second-highest revenue temple in Andhra Pradesh after Tirumala.

name: Simhachalam Temple
town_description: Visakhapatnam (Vizag) is a port city on the Bay of Bengal in coastal Andhra Pradesh and the state's largest city, set between the Eastern Ghats and a long sandy shoreline. It is known for its beaches (Rama Krishna Beach, Rushikonda), the Submarine Museum, and the industrial and naval harbour, and it serves as the gateway to Simhachalam, one of South India's principal Narasimha shrines.

travel.airport: Visakhapatnam International Airport (approx. 13 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Visakhapatnam Junction (approx. 16 km); Simhachalam Railway Station is about 10 km from the hill temple.
travel.road: APSRTC buses run frequently from the Visakhapatnam RTC Complex (Dwaraka Bus Station) to the Simhachalam hilltop bus stand. Vehicles can drive directly to the top; alternatively there are 1,000 stone steps from the base for those who wish to climb.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when coastal Andhra's weather is pleasant. Chandanotsavam on Akshaya Tritiya (April-May) is the one day to see the deity's true form, but expect crowds in the hundreds of thousands; early mornings on weekdays are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM; evening 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM (closed 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM for rituals). Sarva (general) darshan is free; special darshan about Rs. 100 and priority darshan about Rs. 300. Mobile phones and cameras are not allowed inside the temple.
